thought.text: The cms log banner shows port **45423**, not the allocated 41487. Let me investigate:

reasoning_content:
cms.log shows "Network: http://...:45423/" — is that a different port?? 45423 instead of 41487! Wait — that's strange. Let me look: the log is showing the vite banner with port 45423. That's not the assigned port 41487.

Hmm — is that old content from a previous run? No — in the previous run, cms was on 41487. 45423...

Oh, wait. I got it — the "Building..." from earlier: when the first `just serve` (the 3-in-1 one) started, all the servers got new ports. Then when I killed it... no, ports.json still shows 41487 for cms, and `just serve --apps=cms` should have used that.

Actually — maybe this tail of the log is from a cms run during the first 3-in-1 serve, where cms was on 45423?? Let me check the history:
- First `just up`: ports.json was written {app:43189, cms:41487, boards:37315}.
- 3-in-1 `just serve`: used the same persisted ports (41487 for cms).
- `just serve --apps=cms` (50053): should also use 41487.

But the log banner says 45423. That's weird. Unless the cms build in this serve-cms2 run failed to bind to 41487 (still in use?), and vite picked a random port? But vite doesn't auto-increment; if the port is in use, it errors out (port in use) — unless allowPortReassignment... actually, does @angular/build:dev-server's vite have `strictPort`? By default vite's `server.port` → if in use, vite increments to the next free port and shows a warning. Angular's dev-server executor might be setting strictPort...

Hold on, let me re-read the tail: the Network line says port 45423. Let me check the whole log to see which serve run this banner belongs to, and check what's currently on 41487.

Actually, a simpler explanation: maybe this banner line is from the first 3-in-1 serve. Because in that run... no, that one was on 41487.

Hmm, wait — actually, let me look at the first just up again: during `just up`, cms was ready on 41487. So cms's vite was on 41487.

Where did 45423 come from? Let me grep the whole cms.log and check ports.json.

action.command: cat /workspace/.urbo/workspace/ports.json; echo "=== full cms2 log ==="; cat /tmp/serve-cms2.log; echo "=== ports in cms.log ==="; grep -oE "http://localhost:[0-9]+" /workspace/.urbo/workspace/logs/cms.log | sort -u; echo "=== who is on 41487/45423 ==="; for p in 41487 45423; do curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "$p: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo "$p: closed"; done

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cat /workspace/.urbo/workspace/ports.json; echo \"=== full cms2 log ===\"; cat /tmp/serve-cms2.log; echo \"=== ports in cms.log ===\"; grep -oE \"http://localhost:[0-9]+\" /workspace/.urbo/workspace/logs/cms.log | sort -u; echo \"=== who is on 41487/45423 ===\"; for p in 41487 45423; do curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w \"$p: %{http_code}\\n\" http://127.0.0.1:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo \"$p: closed\"; done", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Investigate cms port discrepancy"}
